full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff''''s case, in short, is that, except the land covered by Khatian Nos. 399 and 445 the remaining portion of the suit property belonged to Binode Bihari Das who owned and possessed the same. It was further contended that the suit land was the self-acquired property of Binod Bihari Das. The land of Khatian Nos. 399 and 445 was the ancestral property of the said Binode Bihari Das who had two other full-brothers, namely, Birendre Kumar Das and Bimala Charan Das and the three brothers jointly owned and possessed the same. While being in exclusive possession in the suit property the said Binode Behari Das executed a registered will in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land. Subsequently, the said Binode Behari died in this country in 1962 as a citizen of the erstwhile Pakistan and since his death the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit property peacefully on payment of rent to the Govt. Acquired Estate. It was further contended that the aforesaid will executed by Binode Bihari Das has been duly probated by a competent civil Court and she duly obtained letters of Administration against the said will. The defendants illegally served a notice on her in the later part of 1976 asking her to surrender possession of the suit property as vested property. She thereafter filed an application before the ADC (Rev), Sylhet praying for cancellation of the aforesaid notice but to no effect. It was further contended that as far back as in the year 1972 the matter was taken up for investigation by the Sub-Divisional Officer, who after due enquiry into the matter found that the suit property is not a vested property. The plaintiff contended that she has title and possession in the suit property and, as such, the defendants have no right to disturb her lawful possession by exercising executive powers.
